text:
alex: Observed sustained packet loss to eu-west1 control plane since ~03:10Z. GPU pods stuck in Terminating and many inference workers showing low GPU util but high queue depth (queue ~12k). Alerts from autoscaler and queue depth thresholds firing. /cc @oncall-sre

oncall-sre: Confirmed. health checks to eu-west1 control plane show 502/timeouts. Alerts routed to incidents. Investigating ingress/pathing.

jin: NOC reports intermittent BGP flaps between our backbone and the cloud provider peering starting 03:12Z. They see route churn, some AS paths blackholed. No simple overlay config change fixes it.

maria: We need immediate mitigation to protect global capacity. Proposal: apply temporary per-customer soft caps for the top customers + shift non-geo traffic to us-east. Also enable model-fallback (smaller quantized variant) on affected routes to reduce GPU pressure.

alex: Agreed. List priority customers for soft-caps: cust-phi, acme, memora, deeplytics, lumen, finlyt, astroai. Jin, can we both reroute and set per-customer caps?

jin: Yes. We can push a routing policy to prefer us-east1 for API keys that are not geo-restricted and simultaneously create per-customer rate-limit policies for the geo-locked keys. Rolling now.

alex: Example CLI to create the soft-cap (running now):

```
redwoodctl rate-limit create \
  --region eu-west1 \
  --matcher "customer_id in (cust-phi,acme,memora,deeplytics,lumen,finlyt,astroai)" \
  --softcap 0.4 --burst 0.6 \
  --reason "eu-west network degradation" \
  --expires 2026-03-18T05:10:00Z
```

policy-bot: rate-limit created id=rl_20260318_045, applied to 7 customers. Matched api_keys: [redacted].

ops-sre: Starting traffic shift to us-east1 for non-geo keys. 25% of eligible traffic migrated so far (approx 2.1k rps). Latency on us-east instances looks normal.

maria: Also enabling model-fallback profile "small-llama-q4" on affected route set. Note: this reduces per-token cost and latency but may slightly degrade output fidelity; we should post a support banner.

cs: Drafting status page: "We are experiencing errors and higher latency for customers in EU West due to network connectivity issues. We have applied temporary rate limiting and are shifting traffic to healthy regions. Engineers are working on a fix. Updates every 15 minutes." Will publish after you approve.

alex: Rollback/expansion plan: if packet loss persists >30m, expand soft-caps to top-50 customers and pause noncritical background embedding jobs. Any objections?

ops-sre: No objections. Pausing label=background,priority=low batch jobs now (kubectl patch job ...).

jin: NOC ETA for peering convergence ~45-60m. I'll attach BGP dump and traceroutes here as they update.

oncall-sre: Created incident ticket INC-20260318-44. Next checkpoint at 04:15Z.

alex: Thanks. Summary of actions taken: created rate-limit rl_20260318_045, shifted 25% traffic to us-east, enabled fallback model profile on affected routes, paused low-priority batch jobs. I'll update after 04:15Z.

noc: BGP update: peer X flapped 4x in last 10m, working with provider support.

alex: Good. Keep thread tight — paste exact commands and policy ids only. We'll avoid ad-hoc changes during the window.

cs: Status published. Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2026-03-18/eu-west-network

alex: bravo team.
